0.0.n: Names the creature his sister became.

0.1.n: Marks the resulting state with なる.

0.2.n: Past form of なる; 鬼になった describes 妹 directly.

0.3.n: Specifically means a sister younger than the speaker.

0.4.n: Links the family relationship 妹 to her name, rather than showing possession.

0.5.n: 禰 is the first character of the name 禰豆子, split across two subtitle tokens.

0.6.n: 豆子 completes the name 禰豆子; it does not mean beans here.

0.7.n: Marks Nezuko as the person the speaker wants to change back.

0.9.n: Names the state the speaker wants his sister to return to.

0.10.n: Marks the desired resulting state with 戻す.

0.11.n: 戻す becomes 戻したい with たい, expressing the speaker's wish to restore someone or something.

1.0.n: A casual, masculine way to refer to yourself.

1.1.n: Marks 俺 as the topic: who this statement is about.

1.2.n: Points back to the goal of making Nezuko human again.

1.3.n: Combines with その and に to express acting toward that goal.

1.4.n: Completes そのために, marking the purpose of the speaker's actions.

1.5.n: First part of 鬼殺隊, the name of the Demon Slayer Corps.

1.6.n: Middle character of 鬼殺隊; it is part of the organization's name, not a separate verb here.

1.7.n: Final part of the organization name 鬼殺隊; 隊 denotes an organized unit.

1.8.n: Marks the organization the speaker joined with 入る.

1.9.n: Connecting form of 入る, linking joining the corps to the next action.

1.11.n: Japanese does not mark plural here; the context refers to demons generally.

1.12.n: Identifies the opponents in the fighting.

1.13.n: Lets 鬼と describe 戦い, producing the phrase fighting against demons.

1.14.n: A noun from 戦う, referring to battles against demons.

1.15.n: Marks the activity on which the speaker has staked his life.

1.16.n: Refers to the speaker's own life in the expression 命を懸ける.

1.17.n: Marks 命 as what the speaker risks.

1.18.n: 懸ける in て-form plus きた shows risking his life repeatedly or continuously up to now.

2.0.n: Introduces something the speaker considers obvious or readily acknowledges.

2.2.n: With まで, this refers to the present point in his journey.

2.3.n: Marks 今日 as the endpoint of the period being discussed.

2.4.n: やってくる becomes やってこれた, a casual shortened form of やってこられた expressing past ability to continue.

2.5.n: Turns the preceding action into something that can serve as the sentence's topic.

2.6.n: Marks the whole idea of having made it this far as the topic.

2.8.n: The speaker uses this casual, masculine self-reference again.

2.9.n: Limits the source of strength to the speaker, a limitation the sentence then denies.

2.10.n: Links 俺だけ to 力, identifying whose strength is meant.

2.11.n: Refers to personal ability or effort, not just physical power.

2.12.n: Casual contraction of では; together with ない, it denies the preceding noun phrase.

2.13.n: Completes じゃない, the casual negative ending used after a noun.

0.lit: My younger sister Nezuko, who became a demon, I want to turn back into a human.
0.tip: 戻したい means wanting to restore someone else; 戻りたい would mean wanting to return yourself.

1.lit: I, for that purpose, joined the Demon Slayer Corps and have staked my life on fighting against demons.
1.tip: The てきた ending connects past efforts to the present, emphasizing what the speaker has done up to now.

2.lit: Of course, having managed to keep going until today is not my strength alone.
2.tip: The pattern のは turns the preceding action into a topic, setting up an explanation of what made it possible.
